title: Probabilistic canary primer and pin prototype
content:
Context / goal:
- Personal notebook exploring a different flavour of canary: probabilistic routing + per-client token-bucket smoothing instead of strict cohort buckets. Objective: reduce bursty error/latency exposure while still getting signal quickly. Also capture ideas for version pin heuristics when we do quantization/parameter-change rollouts.

High-level idea (sketch):
1) Every request assigned a per-customer probability p(customer, new_version) that slowly ramps from 0 -> target over time.
2) Probability is driven by two signals: (a) global ramp curve, (b) customer health score (0..1) derived from recent errors/latency/regressions for that tenant. final p = global_curve * customer_health * smoothing_factor.
3) To avoid spikes when a customer jumps from p=0 -> p=0.2, use a token-bucket style admission for the new variant: each tenant has a small token reservoir that refills at rate r, each new-variant decision consumes a token. If no tokens, route to baseline. This flattens short-term bursts from e.g., webhook fanouts or cron jobs.

Why this might help:
- avoids rigid cohort creation (no need to predefine 10% cohort lists)
- per-tenant safety ensures tenants with brittle traffic don't get exposed suddenly
- token-bucket smoothing preserves low-percentile latency budgets because we prevent micro-surges of new-variant traffic

Operational primitives to implement (quick list):
- tenant-health evaluator: lightweight windowed metrics (5m/30m) -> health score. Inputs: error-rate, 95th latency, QPS delta vs historical baseline.
- global ramp controller: timeline + manual override + emergency rollback toggle.
- per-tenant token reservoir: small in-memory counters (durable?) with per-tenant limits to avoid noisy neighbor.
- decision function: deterministic hashing (request id or session) + random draw seeded by day so can reproduce sampling for debugging.

Metrics and telemetry to watch (minimal set):
- per-tenant new-variant ratio (actual traffic vs expected p)
- 95/99 latency delta (new vs baseline) per tenant and global
- error delta (4xx/5xx / model-specific error signals)
- model-output quality signals (if available): BLEU/similarity regressions for eval prompts or production synthetic checks
- token-bucket exhaustion rate per tenant (if >5% indicates we are throttling too much)

Safety and escape hatches:
- auto-fallback: if new-variant error-rate > threshold (absolute or relative to baseline), instantly flip tenant to baseline and mark health=0 for 30m.
- soft pin: ability to pin a tenant to a model version via metadata (client header override or admin API). Pin should be sticky and reasoned (reason + TTL).
- emergency global kill switch (older plan) + day-of-week quiet windows for risky rollouts.

Version pin heuristics (notes):
- pin when a tenant experiences > 3 regressions in 1h after flip and operator confirmation: automatic suggestion to pin with link to first failing request.
- incremental pin TTL: start with 2h, allow extend to 24h after manual review.
- metadata: store pin origin (auto/manual), operator, ticket id, symptoms. Keep as string metadata so we can show in console.

Sample small experiment plan (for next week):
- Week-of experiment: 5 internal tenants (low QPS) as initial seeds. 0 -> 5% over 2h (global_curve linear), token refill 1 token per 10s, reservoir 6 tokens. Watch token exhaustion and latency deltas.
- If stable, widen to 20 tenants and target 10% over 4h.

Edge cases / unresolved questions (todo):
- Persisting token-buckets across service restarts: cheap in-memory vs durable store. Con: in-memory gives restart-induced bursts. Maybe store shallow checkpoint in memcached with TTL.
- Hash determinism: need to ensure sampling reproducible across retries and client retries that might change request ids. Use session id or user id if present; fallback to request id.
- Multi-region routing: how do we coordinate p(customer) across regions? Keep a global control-plane that pushes per-tenant p to region caches, TTL ~30s.
- Interactions with SDK feature flags: when SDK toggles model version, ensure precedence: SDK pin > server pin > probabilistic sampling. Document order of operations.

Quick TODOs for myself: (short actionable list)
- [ ] prototype tenant-health function in notebook (python) using historical traces from last 30 days (we have local sample dataset).
- [ ] write simple sim: 1000 synthetic tenants, traffic patterns (cron spikes, steady QPS, bursty). Simulate token-bucket smoothing and measure 95th latency exposure.
- [ ] sketch console UI: per-tenant "pin" button, per-tenant health chart, token exhaustion markers.
- [ ] draft a short RFC for eng-runtime on probabilistic routing with safety gates. Link to JIRA-1234.

Useful CLI / debugging commands for operators (notes):
- curl to force pin: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" https://console.internal/release/pins -d '{"tenant":"tenant-xyz","version":"v2.3-q8","ttl":"2h","reason":"auto-suggest-failed-regression"}'
- metric query: (promql) sum(rate(new_variant_requests[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(total_requests[5m])) by (tenant) -> per-tenant fraction
- quick rollback: admin API toggle new_variant_enabled=false (global)

Random thoughts / heuristics I like:
- start with conservative token refill (low r) and small reservoir, we can always open the faucet. Too-liberal initial ramp causes confusing noise.
- prefer customer-health weight to be "sticky" for short windows; if a tenant gets marked poor, it should take minutes to recover to avoid oscillation.
- automations should suggest pins but ask for human-in-the-loop for high-impact tenants (top N by revenue).

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally informal. Save formal wording for RFC once prototype sim is promising.

Links / references I keep meaning to read:
- internal: /confluence/runtime/probabilistic-routing (TODO add link)
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/678
- jira: JIRA-1234 (prob-canary prototype)

End of note.
